question: Punch-marked coins from the sixth century BCE onwards were made of silver and which of the following metals?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Punch-marked coins are made up of **silver and copper**.
 
• They are also known as **Aahat coins**.
 
• They are classified into two groups **local and universal**.
 
 
• Local punched marked coins carry **one to four symbols** depending upon their location and size.
 
• Universal punched marked coins carry **five symbols** and are mainly issued by **Magadh Dynasty**.
 
 
 
• The coins were 1st introduced by **Janapadas and Mahajanapadas of the Indo-Gangetic Plain**.
 
• They are created by **hammering **with the help of **punches and dies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Dynasty/Rule**
 **Type of coins**
 
 

 Mauryan Empire
 Punch-marked coins made of silver and copper
 
 

 Indo-Greeks
 Minted coins are made of silver, usually round.

 1st Dynasty introduced a large number of gold coins
 
 

 The Gupta Empire
 Well-minted and well-executed gold coins
